content.text: These Base Terms contain no minimum purchase commitment. Charges are tied to ordered Services and usage, and Customer holds a broad convenience exit. Submitting a compliant finding.

input.quote: Charges for applicable Services will be specified in Service Option Attachments and Order Forms. Charges can be specified as one-time, installment, recurring, or usage. IBM will invoice such Charges when they begin or are due as set forth in Service Option Attachments.
input.rationale: The Base Terms impose no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay, committed volume or shortfall charge on Customer, which meets the preferred position. Searches for "minimum", "commit", "shortfall", "purchase" and "volume" return nothing of the kind: § 4.1 (p0052) prices only ordered Services on a one-time, installment, recurring or usage basis, and § 11.5 Capacity Planning (p0142) allocates capacity forecasting responsibility to Customer without any floor or cap on Customer usage — it lets Customer request changes "as determined by Customer," which is a discretion in our favour rather than a commitment. Customer also has an unconditional exit under § 3.4: termination for convenience of the Agreement or any Service Option Attachment at the end of any calendar month on one month's notice (p0044–p0045), which is more generous than the fallback's 30-day reduction right, and § 3.3 confirms IBM cannot recover early termination charges where IBM has breached. Two diligence notes, not deviations: (i) § 3.4(b) (p0046) conditions the convenience exit on "the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments," and (ii) § 3.5 (p0049) preserves charges under non-terminated Service Option Attachments. Those attachments and Order Forms are not part of the text under review, so any committed spend, minimum volume or termination-charge formula must be checked there when the commercial schedules are issued; the mechanics in the Base Terms themselves are compliant. No redline proposed.
